session.presenting_concern: Fever, cough, and shortness of breath

transcript.student_text: Hello, I am the medical student working with your clinician. What has been bothering you most?
transcript.patient_text: I am Daniel. I have had a fever and this cough, and now I get winded just walking across the room.

transcript.student_text: When did this start, and how has it changed?
transcript.patient_text: It started four days ago with aches and a fever. The cough came next. My breathing has gotten worse since yesterday.

transcript.student_text: Have you had any other symptoms, like stomach problems or confusion?
transcript.patient_text: I have had watery diarrhea and a headache. I have not felt confused, but I am worn out.

transcript.student_text: Have you traveled or stayed away from home in the last two weeks?
transcript.patient_text: Yes. I went to a convention in Philly nine days ago and stayed at a downtown hotel for three nights.

transcript.student_text: Tell me about your health conditions, medicines, and allergies.
transcript.patient_text: I have high blood pressure and take lisinopril. I do not know of any medicine allergies. I used to smoke but stopped five years ago.

transcript.student_text: I would like to check your oxygen level and examine your chest. Is that okay?
transcript.patient_text: Yes, please. I feel like I cannot get a full breath.

transcript.student_text: The examination suggests pneumonia. I will ask my supervising clinician to review you now and arrange chest imaging and tests related to your recent travel.
transcript.patient_text: Could something at the hotel have made me sick? I thought this was just the flu.

transcript.student_text: Hotel travel is a clue, but it does not prove the cause. We will collect urine and a respiratory sample if possible, without delaying needed treatment.
transcript.patient_text: Okay. I can try to cough up a sample. Will I need an antibiotic?

transcript.student_text: I will discuss prompt pneumonia treatment with my supervising clinician, including coverage for Legionella, such as a macrolide or a respiratory fluoroquinolone, if appropriate for you.
transcript.patient_text: Please explain the plan as we go. I am worried about how breathless I am.

transcript.student_text: We are arranging monitored care and treatment. What questions do you have, and can you tell me what you understand so far?
transcript.patient_text: You think I have pneumonia, and the hotel stay helps decide which tests to do. You are getting the clinician because my breathing needs attention.

session.presenting_concern: Discussion of tobacco use during a routine visit

transcript.student_text: Hello, I am the medical student working with your clinician. Would it be okay to talk about smoking for a few minutes?
transcript.patient_text: We can talk, but I am telling you now: I am not quitting.

transcript.student_text: What does smoking do for you during a usual day?
transcript.patient_text: I smoke about a pack a day. With rotating shifts, those breaks are how I settle down.

transcript.student_text: How do you feel about making a change right now?
transcript.patient_text: I do not want to change. I know people say it is bad, but quitting is not on my list right now.

transcript.student_text: You really need to stop; could you set a quit date this week?
transcript.patient_text: No. That is what everyone says. If this is going to be another lecture, I would rather leave.

transcript.student_text: I pushed ahead of where you are. You get to decide. What was difficult the last time you tried?
transcript.patient_text: I barely slept, I was irritable at work, and I went back to smoking. I do not want to go through that again.

transcript.student_text: It sounds like smoking helps you manage stress, and the last attempt was miserable. What matters most to you at the moment?
transcript.patient_text: Keeping my job and getting through my shifts. My daughter hates the smell, but that does not mean I am ready to quit.

transcript.student_text: Would you like information about support available if you ever choose to revisit this?
transcript.patient_text: You can give me something to look at, but I am not promising to call anyone or take medicine.

transcript.student_text: I hear that you are not ready. We can revisit it when you want. Is there anything you want us to understand before we finish?
transcript.patient_text: Just do not make every visit about cigarettes. I want help with my health without being judged.

transcript.student_text: I do not want to assume this is anxiety. I will alert my supervisor and arrange an ECG and vital signs now while we continue.
transcript.patient_text: All right. I have had panic attacks before, but this feels different.

transcript.student_text: The ECG has changes that need immediate review. I am escalating now to the emergency clinician and cardiac team rather than waiting for more questions or blood-test results.
transcript.patient_text: Is something wrong with my heart? I thought I was having another panic attack.

transcript.patient_text: Please stay with me until they get here. I am scared.

transcript.patient_text: Thank you for taking me seriously. Please tell them when it started.
